The '''2024–25 Minnesota Frost season''' was the team's second season as a member of the [[Professional Women's Hockey League]].  They played their home games at the [[Grand Casino Arena|Xcel Energy Center]] in [[Saint Paul, Minnesota]]. The Frost defeated the [[Toronto Sceptres]] in the semifinals of the [[2025 PWHL playoffs]] to advance to the [[2025 PWHL Finals]]. During the Finals they defeated the [[Ottawa Charge]] to win their second consecutive [[Walter Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/pwhl/article/minnesota-frost-capture-second-walter-cup-title/ |title=Minnesota Frost capture second Walter Cup title |website=Sportsnet |date=May 26, 2025 |access-date=May 26, 2025}}</ref>

== Offseason ==

* On June 7, 2024, one week after winning the league's inaugural championship and with only days before the draft, it was reported the general manager [[Natalie Darwitz]] would not return for the 2024–25 season.  Darwitz was instead offered alternative options within the league.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/pwhl/article/report-natalie-darwitz-out-as-gm-of-pwhl-minnesota/ |title=Report: Natalie Darwitz out as GM of PWHL Minnesota |website=sportsnet.ca |date=June 7, 2024 |quote=Just eight days after Minnesota won the PWHL’s first-ever Walter Cup championship, general manager Natalie Darwitz is reportedly departing the organization. |access-date=June 7, 2024 |archive-date=June 7, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240607151642/https://www.sportsnet.ca/pwhl/article/report-natalie-darwitz-out-as-gm-of-pwhl-minnesota/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Regular season===

The regular season schedule was announced on October 15, 2024. The Frost's season will begin on December 1, 2024, and will end on May 3, 2025, with each team playing 30 games; six games against every opponent.<ref name="season-schedule">{{cite web |title=2024–25 Schedule |url=https://www.thepwhl.com/en/stats/schedule/all-teams/5/all-months?league=1 |access-date=October 17, 2024 |website=thepwhl.com |publisher=[[Professional Women's Hockey League]] |archive-date=November 7, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241107024814/https://www.thepwhl.com/en/stats/schedule/all-teams/5/all-months?league=1 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://thehockeynews.com/womens/pwhl/eight-cities-to-host-stops-on-the-pwhl-takeover-tour-including-west-coast |title=Eight Cities To Host Stops On The PWHL Takeover Tour Including West Coast |last=Kennedy |first=Ian |date=November 18, 2024 |website=TheHockeyNews.com |publisher=[[The Hockey News]] |access-date=November 18, 2024 |quote=Buffalo, Denver, Detroit, Raleigh, St. Louis and Seattle to host U.S. games; Québec City and Vancouver will serve as Canadian Stops on the PWHL's 2024–25 Takeover Tour. |archive-date=November 18, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241118215417/https://thehockeynews.com/womens/pwhl/eight-cities-to-host-stops-on-the-pwhl-takeover-tour-including-west-coast |url-status=live }}</ref>

{{legend2|#fff|Overtime/shootout loss (1 point)|border=1px solid black}}
{{legend2|#fcc|Regulation Loss (0 points)|border=1px solid black}}
{{Game log end}}

=== Playoffs ===

{{main|2025 PWHL playoffs}}

On May 4, the first-place [[Montreal Victoire]] announced that they chose to play the third-place [[Ottawa Charge]] in the first round.  This decision meant that fourth-place Minnesota would play the second-place [[Toronto Sceptres]] in a re-match of last year's semi-finals.<ref name="montreal-playoff-selection">{{YouTube|i3S8QFMJNeQ|Playoff Opponent Selection LIVE with Jocks in Jills}}</ref><ref name="pwhl-playoff-schedule">{{cite web |url=https://www.thepwhl.com/en/news/2025/may/04/pwhl-announces-playoff-matchups-and-schedule |title=PWHL Announces Playoff Matchups and Schedule |date=May 4, 2025 |website=ThePWHL.com |publisher=[[Professional Women's Hockey League]] |access-date=May 4, 2025 |quote=''Montréal selected Ottawa as its semifinal opponent, Toronto to play Minnesota''}}</ref>
